name: StampBatch — Batch Photo Watermark & Re-Check (Text & Logo, Local, Private)
description:
My photos keep getting reposted without my name on them, usually the week I finally start selling — how do I watermark them in batch?
StampBatch watermarks a whole folder of photos in one run — your text or your logo — then RE-OPENS every output and pixel-compares it against the original, so you can prove each mark landed and nothing else about the photo changed.
WHAT IT DOES
• Text watermarks (white or black) or your own logo image, transparency respected
• Nine-grid positioning: any corner, edge-centre, or dead centre
• Opacity and relative-size controls — the mark scales correctly from a thumbnail to a 3000px master
• Tiled mode: repeat the mark across the whole frame for proof/preview images
• Platform presets for Etsy and Instagram that pre-tune mark size and margin (presets advise size and margin only — they never alter your photo)
• A re-check report (stamp_report.md) with every batch: per-photo size match + watermark verification
• Originals are never modified — output goes to a separate folder
WHAT IT NEVER DOES
StampBatch only watermarks. It does not resize, crop, rename or convert your photos, so it can't silently degrade or re-frame them — output dimensions are always identical to the input, and the re-check proves it.
VERIFIED, NOT VIBES
Seeded acceptance test: 4 photos (1200×800, 800×1200, 3000×2000, 200×150; JPG + PNG) plus a seed logo, three batches (text corner mark with the Etsy preset, logo mark, tiled text mark). 24 of 24 checks passed — every output re-opened at exactly its original size; watermark-area pixels changed 4.7% (text) / 40.6% (logo) / 7.4% (tiled); opposite corners 0.0% changed; originals' SHA-256 hashes unchanged after all runs.
100% LOCAL & PRIVATE — no upload, no account, no subscription. Your photos never leave your computer.
Windows 10/11, no other software needed. Supports JPG, PNG, WebP, BMP, TIFF. You get the watermarked copies + a plain-English batch report.
Honest limit: a watermark is a deterrent — it raises the cost of stealing your images. It cannot make theft impossible, and anyone who promises otherwise is guessing.
